sections.html:
Utah's second largest city by population is West Valley City, an inner suburb on the valley's northwest side. Salt Lake City borders it north, South Salt Lake east, Magna west, and Taylorsville and Kearns south. The Oquirrh Mountains stand to the west and the Jordan River forms the east boundary.

There were 140,230 residents in 2020, a rise of 8.3% over the 129,480 of 2010, and the newest estimate is 137,491. Of 42,001 housing units in 2020, just 2.9% sat empty. Four communities, Hunter, Granger, Chesterfield and Redwood, merged to form the city in 1980. Building surged in the 1970s, so a lot of the housing is decades old.

Local shorthand splits the city into three areas, and the typical house differs in each.

  • East (Redwood, Chesterfield and East Granger): mostly brick ranch houses from the 1960s and 1970s, near Valley Fair Mall and the Maverik Center. The Westshire area south of the mall has 160 mid-century modern homes built in the 1960s and 1970s.
  • Central (West Granger and Hunter south of 3100 South, with Lakepark and Westlake Business Park to the north): includes the planned Highbury development in the northwest part.
  • West (West Hunter, Woodhaven and Oquirrh): mostly planned developments from the 1990s and 2000s.

East side sellers usually have a brick ranch that is 50 or 60 years old, so what the roof, plumbing and wiring look like sets the price. In the planned West developments, layout and condition count for more.

Interstate 215, State Route 172 (5600 West) and State Route 171 (3500 South) are the main roads. An intermodal hub operated by the Utah Transit Authority is in the city, and the TRAX Green Line stops at West Valley Central.

The 3500 South MAX bus rapid transit line serves the area, and the Midvalley Express links West Valley Central and 2700 West to Taylorsville and on to Murray Central station. Commuters shopping for a house want to know the distance to the interstate and the nearest station.

West Valley City lies in the Granite School District, home to Granger High School and Hunter High School. Which schools a particular house feeds depends on its address, so the district can answer that before you write your listing.

A landlord in West Valley City must hold a current city business license for each rental dwelling. One license can cover several units when the owner hands the city a complete, up-to-date unit list and pays the fees. Co-owners share liability for those fees and any penalties.

The code also sets a rental nuisance standard: more than two police calls for one rental unit in 12 months counts as excessive. An unresolved notice of violation is one with no recorded notice of compliance. Ordinance enforcement handles abatement of unsightly or hazardous property and rental licensing.

  • Renew a lapsed rental license before you list.
  • Resolve any open notice of violation and record the notice of compliance.
  • Pull together the unit list if the city has more than one of your rentals.

The county wants its property tax by November 30 and treats leftovers as delinquent starting December 1. Bills are mailed by November 1. If you dispute your value, you have a 45-day window that runs August 1 to September 15. A tax sale is held in late May for parcels delinquent over five years.

Because of the 45% exemption, tax on a primary residence applies to 55% of market value. Second residences and vacant houses lose that break and are taxed on the full value, which makes an empty inherited house pricier to hold.

At closing the title company prorates the current year's tax, and any balance still owed comes out of your proceeds.

File the deed with the Salt Lake County Recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, for a flat $40.00. Include the parcel number and the buyer's mailing address, and have the deed notarized. City code relies on this office's ownership records when it identifies an owner.

Summers peak near 94.0 degrees in July and winter days top out near 38.6 in January, going by Salt Lake City records. Add about 15.5 inches of precipitation and sharp winter inversions, and roofs and HVAC equipment take a beating. Older ranch houses show it first.

Do your own walk-through before a buyer's inspector does. Check the roof, furnace, air conditioner and water heater, and take a hard look at the electrical panel and aging pipes if the house dates to the 1960s or 1970s.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a West Valley City house
sections.html:
Sellers can list with an agent, go it alone or ask for a cash offer. Cash Home Buyers purchases houses here as they stand, older ranch houses needing updates included. Ask for a number, see how we got to it, and then make up your own mind.

Cash tends to fit a rental with a tenant you are tired of managing, a house carrying code violations, an inherited property or a short fuse. An agent listing is better when the house is in good repair and you can wait out showings and a buyer's loan approval.

A traditional sale usually means cleaning for showings, answering the buyer's repair requests after the inspection, and waiting for a lender to approve the loan. A cash sale skips those steps. The buyer takes the house as it is, so you do not need to repaint, replace an old furnace or finish work that was left half done. The closing date is something you and the buyer settle together, and it is not tied to a loan committee.

That matters for owners of rentals, estates and houses with open code problems, because they often cannot spend months on repairs. You still owe whatever is owed on the property, such as a mortgage or unpaid tax, but those payoffs are handled out of the proceeds at the table. Ask for a written payoff from each lender or office before closing day so nothing surprises you when the final numbers arrive.

Once you accept, a title company requests payoff figures, apportions the property tax, drafts the deed and sends it to the Recorder. Have the deed and your newest tax notice ready, and for a rental add the business license and unit list. An open notice of violation should get its notice of compliance recorded first, or it may stall the sale.

faqs.q: What county is West Valley City in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Property tax, valuation appeals and deed recording go through county offices in Salt Lake City.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in West Valley City?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County property tax is due November 30, and delinquency starts December 1. Notices are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a house in West Valley City?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of rental dwelling units need a current West Valley City business license. Owners of several units can use one license with a list of the units.

faqs.q: Which school district serves West Valley City?
faqs.a: The Granite School District. Granger High School and Hunter High School are in the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Valley City house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is, and many owners of older ranch houses use a cash sale to avoid paying for repairs before closing.
